entities.summary:
Eustochia Smeralda Calafato was a Franciscan Italian saint belonging to the Order of the Poor Clares, co-patroness of Messina and the centre of her cultus.


Calafato was born into a noble family in Messina, Sicily, around 1445, and was raised in a devoutly Catholic household. She joined the Order of the Poor Clares at a young age and dedicated her life to prayer, charity, and education. Calafato's piety and kindness earned her the respect and admiration of her community, and she became a beloved figure in Messina's religious and social life. Despite facing opposition from her family, who wanted her to marry and secure her family's social status, Calafato remained devoted to her vows and continued to serve the poor and marginalized. She died on January 20, 1485, and was canonized as a saint in 1606.


Calafato's legacy extends beyond her own time and place, inspiring generations of Christians and women in particular. Her commitment to education and social justice continues to be celebrated and emulated today, and her example serves as a powerful reminder of the transformative power of faith and compassion.
